subject: Clarify keystore custody & jurisdiction controls for Private Deploy (DPA review)
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acadiahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Acadia Health Legal <dpa@acadiahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA / keystore custody for private deployment

Hi Irene,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft. Our security and legal team raised a few follow-up questions specific to private deployments (VPC/on-prem) where customers manage keys:

- We need clarity on operator access: will Redwood personnel ever have the ability to decrypt customer-provided keys or access plaintext model inputs/outputs for private deployments?
- Jurisdictional transfers: if the customer configures on-prem or a US VPC but certain telemetry or operator-run diagnostics run from EU-hosted control plane nodes, how is that telemetry scoped? Is there a guarantee that key material or plaintext never traverses non-US regions?
- Key escrow/escrow exceptions: can Redwood require an escrow for breakglass? If so, what are the conditions and the access control/audit trail?

I've attached the annotated DPA where we've highlighted clauses; happy to do a short call if that's easier.

Regards,
Maria Gonzalez
Senior Counsel, Acadia Health
Attachments: DPA_Redlines_Acadia.pdf (annotation stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: Acadia Health Legal <dpa@acadiahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA / keystore custody for private deployment

Hi Maria — thanks for the detailed questions and the annotated DPA. I pulled in Karthik from our infra/privacy thread and Marissa from Legal. Quick answers up front, and I included a small keystore handshake diagram for reference (attached).

1) Operator access: for Private Deploy (VPC or on-prem BYOK) the default is customer-controlled keys. Redwood does NOT persist customer plaintext keys. Our operators cannot decrypt customer data unless a customer explicitly grants a one-time breakglass authorization (rare, auditable — see below). We can run diagnostics against encrypted envelopes and metadata.

2) Telemetry/jurisdiction: control plane telemetry (metrics, error traces) is minimized and redacted by default. Any telemetry that could contain identifiers is routed per deployment region policy; for US VPCs we will configure control-plane endpoints in US regions only. We can add contract language that telemetry endpoints for Acadia’s deployments will be US-only unless you request otherwise in writing.

3) Escrow / breakglass: Redwood prefers a deterministic, auditable breakglass process: customer-initiated access via time-limited key escrow release requires a signed request from your security officer and an internal two-person operator approval. All access is logged, 3rd-party audit-ready, and we can include conditions in the DPA. Alternatively, if you prefer we can support customer-held escrows (custodial provider) where Redwood never stores the escrowed secret.

Next steps: Karthik — can you add a short note on the technical controls for the breakglass flow and evidence we will provide (telemetry/audit log excerpts)? Marissa — can you propose the exact DPA language for the telemetry/geofence and breakglass paragraph? Maria — would you prefer Redwood-held breakglass with strict SLAs/audit or a customer escrow solution?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: DPA_draft_Acadia_v1.2.pdf, keystore_handshake_diagram.png

Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA / keystore custody for private deployment

Hi Maria/Irene — quick technical summary to support the DPA language:

- Key handling: In BYOK flows we accept a wrapped key blob. The customer’s CMK (customer-managed key) is used to unwrap locally (on customer infra or in a dedicated HSM you control). We only see a minimal derived envelope (HMAC + encrypted key material) and never the unwrapped plaintext CMK.
- Breakglass: we can support two modes: (a) Redwood-temporary unwrapping in an HSM under strict access controls (requires joint authorization), or (b) customer escrow via an approved custodian (we never touch the escrow). Mode (b) offers the strongest isolation and is recommended for regulated PHI clients.
- Telemetry: diagnostic traces include request identifiers and latency histograms; payloads are NEVER captured. We can provide a sanitized telemetry export for compliance review.

I'll add suggested text for the DPA: 1) explicit prohibition on Redwood personnel decrypting customer-provided key material except under documented breakglass requests; 2) geofencing clause requiring control-plane telemetry endpoints to remain in customer-specified region; 3) audit log retention and sample format.

If it helps, I can draft a short annex to the DPA that spells out the operator access and escrow alternatives.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acadiahealth.com>

Cc: Acadia Health Legal <dpa@acadiahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA / keystore custody for private deployment

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from Legal:

- We need contractual language that explicitly states: "Redwood personnel shall not have access to unencrypted customer key material or plaintext customer content for private deployments unless customer issues a documented breakglass authorization." That sentence should be in the DPA rather than just an appendix.
- For breakglass, Acadia’s policy requires (i) a documented business justification, (ii) pre-approved list of Redwood operator roles that may act, and (iii) joint notarization/audit with forensic snapshots. Is Redwood able to commit to a time-limited access window (e.g., max 4 hours) and provide immediate export of audit logs and snapshots to Acadia?
- Finally, because we are a regulated healthcare provider, we want the preferred escrow option to be customer-controlled escrow with Redwood never holding any escrow keys. If Redwood needs to perform support that would require key release, we prefer a process that enables customer to temporarily provision a decryption token via their custodian.

Please mark up the DPA with proposed language for the first bullet and the breakglass SLA. We're aiming to finalize this before our procurement window in mid-August.

Regards,
Maria

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA / keystore custody for private deployment

Maria — appreciate the specificity. We updated the DPA draft and added an operational annex that covers both Redwood-temporary and customer-custodied escrow flows. Summary of inbound changes we propose:

- Inline clause in Section 4.2: "Redwood personnel shall not access unencrypted customer key material or plaintext customer content for Private Deployments, except pursuant to a documented breakglass authorization initiated by the customer and approved by Redwood under the process set forth in Annex A."
- Annex A: breakglass process: customer request -> verification by customer's pre-authorized security officer -> Redwood double-approval (two operator roles listed) -> time-limited HSM unwrapping window (max 4 hours) -> immediate export of audit logs and forensics delivered to customer via secure link.
- Geofence clause: control-plane telemetry endpoints for Acadia deployments will be restricted to US-hosted endpoints; any telemetry export crossing borders requires written customer approval.

We also added language that if Acadia elects customer-custodied escrow, Redwood will not hold escrow keys and will require evidence of escrow provider SLAs and access procedures.

Attached is DPA_draft_Acadia_v1.3.pdf with tracked changes and a minor update to the handshake diagram. If that addresses your procurement checkbox, Marissa and I can prepare the DocuSign envelope and a short summary for procurement.

If you want another quick sync, we can do 30 minutes Friday morning. Otherwise, we'll circulate the DocuSign link and the annex.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
